# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

Excellent! Now I have the actual failure. This is NOT a timing flake in the sense of gh-937 (settling before capture). Look at the failure:

```
Expected: [
  '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
]
Actual: ['⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older']
Which: at location [0] is '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older' instead of '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
```

The COUNTS are identical — the row text is identical apart from TRAILING WHITESPACE. The `before` capture had the row padded to the full width with trailing spaces (`· older` + trailing spaces to fill the 120-column glass), while the `mid` capture has the row WITHOUT trailing padding.

This happens at line 241 of the test — the `mid.where(...)` equals `beforeOlder` assertion.

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... Let me think about the vendored xterm package behavior.

Actually in the `xterm` Dart package (vendored), `BufferLine` cells: erased cells vs written spaces may differ in `getText()` output? Usually `getText()` joins cell content chars; erased cells are spaces too, so both would give trailing spaces. Hmm, but the actual output shows NO trailing spaces in `mid`.

Wait — actually re-reading: Actual row has NO trailing spaces. Expected (before) has trailing spaces. So in `before`, the `· older` row was written with padding to full width; in `mid`, the row ended right after `· older` and nothing else was ever written on that row beyond that point (the rest of the buffer line was never written with spaces NOR cleared).

How can that be? The TUI repaint: full frame redraw each frame. The frame writes every row. When the board region shrinks (e.g., a settle notice removed a row?), the renderer might redraw only the changed lines and clear the remainder of a line with EL where needed, or it uses relative cursor movements to update rows in place (diff-based rendering, like dart_tui).

Let me think about the frame flow:

`before` was captured right after `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` following wave two's turn (frame complete, full repaint: all rows padded to 120 columns? Not necessarily all — the TUI's diff renderer writes only what changed but pads/clears changed rows to erase previous content).

Then the first settle happens: `[bash] sh-1-… exited(0)` notice is appended to the transcript → the frame scrolls / repaints. The `· older` row moves up by a line (the settle notice added a line above). In the new frame, the `· older` row is written WITHOUT trailing padding — because the diff renderer only wrote the changed cells (the row text), leaving the rest of the buffer line as it was (which contained... hmm, that would PRESERVE the old padding).

Unless the whole frame scrolled: when new lines are appended at the bottom, everything scrolls up by N lines. Scrolling in the xterm emulator: `buffer.lines` shift — the top line is moved to scrollback. When a line scrolls, its content (cells) stays the same. So padding would be preserved...

Wait, actually, look more carefully: in the `before` frame, the `· older` row had trailing spaces to 120 chars. In `mid`, the row has none. The row content is the same. So between before and mid, the row was REWRITTEN without padding, or the line was cleared and rewritten.

Hmm, but wait — is this really the same physical row? The screen scrolled up by ~2 lines (the settle notice block). The `· older` row in `mid` is a different buffer line — one that previously held something else. When the TUI repainted after the settle, it wrote the board row at the new position. If the renderer wrote `⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` and then cleared to end of line with EL, the emulator's erase would fill the rest with blank cells — which in getText() give spaces. If the renderer did NOT clear to EOL (e.g., it knew the old row at this position had exactly the same length? no...).

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider: does `getText()` on the vendored xterm produce trailing spaces for erased cells? Let me check the vendored xterm implementation. In the xterm.dart package, `BufferLine` has `_buffer` with char codes and `getText()` builds from each cell's char. A "blank" cell (erased) has char code of space (0x20)? If the cell is "unwritten" initially, the line may not be materialized at full width — the line tracks `isWrapped`/length? Let me look at the actual package.

Also there's another possibility: the TUI's renderer for the job board region uses `\x1b[K` after each line vs not. Or the renderer writes lines and pads them with spaces to full width only in SOME cases (e.g., when the line is part of the "live region" bottom panel vs the scrolling transcript).

The key question: why does the same logical row sometimes have trailing padding and sometimes not, on macOS but not linux?

Actually, wait. Let me re-read the failing assertion more carefully. Test line 241:

```dart

    .where((l) => l.contains('· older') && l.contains('(5)'))
    .toList();
expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1), reason: 'frame before:\n$before');
await harness.waitForText(_firstSettle, timeout: ...);
await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 300);
final mid = harness.viewportLines;
expectComposerReserved(mid, columns);
expect(
  mid.where((l) => l.contains('· older') && l.contains('(5)')).toList(),
  beforeOlder,
  reason: 'the printed `· older` row never changes counts while its jobs settle ...',
);
```

Line 241 is the `expect(mid.where(...), beforeOlder, ...)`. Both frames contain exactly ONE such row. The only difference: trailing spaces.

So the flake is a pure whitespace-of-buffer-cell artifact: the logical row is identical; the buffer-cell padding differs. On linux, the repaint after the settle notice produced the padded row; on macOS (different timing), the row got repainted in a way that left unpadded cells (or the line simply never got rewritten and the old line at the new scroll position wasn't padded).

Root cause class: the assertion compares raw `getText()` strings including emulator-cell padding, which is an artifact of how the TUI renderer erases/rewrites rows, not of the board's freeze semantics. The freeze assertion should compare TRIMMED content (the counts), not raw padded cells.

But wait — the test is intentionally strict ("byte-identical"). The point is the frozen snapshot must not change counts. Comparing `trimRight()`-ed lines would still catch count changes while ignoring renderer-erase artifacts. But is trimming right? Let me think about whether the trailing-space difference can hide a REAL bug. The `· older` row content is the counts; trailing padding is not content. Trimming trailing whitespace is the correct content comparison.

But hold on — is this purely a test-side artifact, or is there a real product bug where the row is repainted (unfrozen)? The counts in the row are identical ("5 running · 0 done · 0 lost") — so the freeze logic worked. The only difference is buffer padding. Let me look at the TUI rendering for the job board: lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart, and how "live region" lines are drawn.

- `before`: full frame after wave-two turn completed. Frame rows include the board region: `⟳ Bac…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no

Excellent! Now I have the actual failure. This is NOT a timing flake in the sense of gh-937 (settling before capture). Look at the failure:

```
Expected: [
  '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
]
Actual: ['⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older']
Which: at location [0] is '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older' instead of '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
```

The COUNTS are identical — the row text is identical apart from TRAILING WHITESPACE. The `before` capture had the row padded to the full width with trailing spaces (`· older` + trailing spaces to fill the 120-column glass), while the `mid` capture has the row WITHOUT trailing padding.

This happens at line 241 of the test — the `mid.where(...)` equals `beforeOlder` assertion.

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... Let me think about the vendored xterm package behavior.

Actually in the `xterm` Dart package (vendored), `BufferLine` cells: erased cells vs written spaces may differ in `getText()` output? Usually `getText()` joins cell content chars; erased cells are spaces too, so both would give trailing spaces. Hmm, but the actual output shows NO trailing spaces in `mid`.

Wait — actually re-reading: Actual row has NO trailing spaces. Expected (before) has trailing spaces. So in `before`, the `· older` row was written with padding to full width; in `mid`, the row ended right after `· older` and nothing else was ever written on that row beyond that point (the rest of the buffer line was never written with spaces NOR cleared).

How can that be? The TUI repaint: full frame redraw each frame. The frame writes every row. When the board region shrinks (e.g., a settle notice removed a row?), the renderer might redraw only the changed lines and clear the remainder of a line with EL where needed, or it uses relative cursor movements to update rows in place (diff-based rendering, like dart_tui).

Let me think about the frame flow:

`before` was captured right after `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` following wave two's turn (frame complete, full repaint: all rows padded to 120 columns? Not necessarily all — the TUI's diff renderer writes only what changed but pads/clears changed rows to erase previous content).

Then the first settle happens: `[bash] sh-1-… exited(0)` notice is appended to the transcript → the frame scrolls / repaints. The `· older` row moves up by a line (the settle notice added a line above). In the new frame, the `· older` row is written WITHOUT trailing padding — because the diff renderer only wrote the changed cells (the row text), leaving the rest of the buffer line as it was (which contained... hmm, that would PRESERVE the old padding).

Unless the whole frame scrolled: when new lines are appended at the bottom, everything scrolls up by N lines. Scrolling in the xterm emulator: `buffer.lines` shift — the top line is moved to scrollback. When a line scrolls, its content (cells) stays the same. So padding would be preserved...

Wait, actually, look more carefully: in the `before` frame, the `· older` row had trailing spaces to 120 chars. In `mid`, the row has none. The row content is the same. So between before and mid, the row was REWRITTEN without padding, or the line was cleared and rewritten.

Hmm, but wait — is this really the same physical row? The screen scrolled up by ~2 lines (the settle notice block). The `· older` row in `mid` is a different buffer line — one that previously held something else. When the TUI repainted after the settle, it wrote the board row at the new position. If the renderer wrote `⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` and then cleared to end of line with EL, the emulator's erase would fill the rest with blank cells — which in getText() give spaces. If the renderer did NOT clear to EOL (e.g., it knew the old row at this position had exactly the same length? no...).

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider: does `getText()` on the vendored xterm produce trailing spaces for erased cells? Let me check the vendored xterm implementation. In the xterm.dart package, `BufferLine` has `_buffer` with char codes and `getText()` builds from each cell's char. A "blank" cell (erased) has char code of space (0x20)? If the cell is "unwritten" initially, the line may not be materialized at full width — the line tracks `isWrapped`/length? Let me look at the actual package.

Also there's another possibility: the TUI's renderer for the job board region uses `\x1b[K` after each line vs not. Or the renderer writes lines and pads them with spaces to full width only in SOME cases (e.g., when the line is part of the "live region" bottom panel vs the scrolling transcript).

The key question: why does the same logical row sometimes have trailing padding and sometimes not, on macOS but not linux?

Actually, wait. Let me re-read the failing assertion more carefully. Test line 241:

```dart
final beforeOlder = before
    .where((l) => l.contains('· older') && l.contains('(5)'))
    .toList();
expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1), reason: 'frame before:\n$before');

So the flake is a pure whitespace-of-buffer-cell artifact: the logical row is identical; the buffer-cell padding differs. On linux, the repaint after the settle notice produced the padded row; on macOS (different timing), the row got repainted in a way that left unpadded cells (or the line simply never got rewritten and the old line at the new scroll position wasn't padded).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

Excellent! Now I have the actual failure. This is NOT a timing flake in the sense of gh-937 (settling before capture). Look at the failure:

```
Expected: [
  '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
]
Actual: ['⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older']
Which: at location [0] is '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older' instead of '⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older                                                             '
```

The COUNTS are identical — the row text is identical apart from TRAILING WHITESPACE. The `before` capture had the row padded to the full width with trailing spaces (`· older` + trailing spaces to fill the 120-column glass), while the `mid` capture has the row WITHOUT trailing padding.

This happens at line 241 of the test — the `mid.where(...)` equals `beforeOlder` assertion.

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... Let me think about the vendored xterm package behavior.

Actually in the `xterm` Dart package (vendored), `BufferLine` cells: erased cells vs written spaces may differ in `getText()` output? Usually `getText()` joins cell content chars; erased cells are spaces too, so both would give trailing spaces. Hmm, but the actual output shows NO trailing spaces in `mid`.

Wait — actually re-reading: Actual row has NO trailing spaces. Expected (before) has trailing spaces. So in `before`, the `· older` row was written with padding to full width; in `mid`, the row ended right after `· older` and nothing else was ever written on that row beyond that point (the rest of the buffer line was never written with spaces NOR cleared).

How can that be? The TUI repaint: full frame redraw each frame. The frame writes every row. When the board region shrinks (e.g., a settle notice removed a row?), the renderer might redraw only the changed lines and clear the remainder of a line with EL where needed, or it uses relative cursor movements to update rows in place (diff-based rendering, like dart_tui).

Let me think about the frame flow:

`before` was captured right after `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` following wave two's turn (frame complete, full repaint: all rows padded to 120 columns? Not necessarily all — the TUI's diff renderer writes only what changed but pads/clears changed rows to erase previous content).

Then the first settle happens: `[bash] sh-1-… exited(0)` notice is appended to the transcript → the frame scrolls / repaints. The `· older` row moves up by a line (the settle notice added a line above). In the new frame, the `· older` row is written WITHOUT trailing padding — because the diff renderer only wrote the changed cells (the row text), leaving the rest of the buffer line as it was (which contained... hmm, that would PRESERVE the old padding).

Unless the whole frame scrolled: when new lines are appended at the bottom, everything scrolls up by N lines. Scrolling in the xterm emulator: `buffer.lines` shift — the top line is moved to scrollback. When a line scrolls, its content (cells) stays the same. So padding would be preserved...

Wait, actually, look more carefully: in the `before` frame, the `· older` row had trailing spaces to 120 chars. In `mid`, the row has none. The row content is the same. So between before and mid, the row was REWRITTEN without padding, or the line was cleared and rewritten.

Hmm, but wait — is this really the same physical row? The screen scrolled up by ~2 lines (the settle notice block). The `· older` row in `mid` is a different buffer line — one that previously held something else. When the TUI repainted after the settle, it wrote the board row at the new position. If the renderer wrote `⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` and then cleared to end of line with EL, the emulator's erase would fill the rest with blank cells — which in getText() give spaces. If the renderer did NOT clear to EOL (e.g., it knew the old row at this position had exactly the same length? no...).

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider: does `getText()` on the vendored xterm produce trailing spaces for erased cells? Let me check the vendored xterm implementation. In the xterm.dart package, `BufferLine` has `_buffer` with char codes and `getText()` builds from each cell's char. A "blank" cell (erased) has char code of space (0x20)? If the cell is "unwritten" initially, the line may not be materialized at full width — the line tracks `isWrapped`/length? Let me look at the actual package.

Also there's another possibility: the TUI's renderer for the job board region uses `\x1b[K` after each line vs not. Or the renderer writes lines and pads them with spaces to full width only in SOME cases (e.g., when the line is part of the "live region" bottom panel vs the scrolling transcript).

The key question: why does the same logical row sometimes have trailing padding and sometimes not, on macOS but not linux?

Actually, wait. Let me re-read the failing assertion more carefully. Test line 241:

```dart
final beforeOlder = before
    .where((l) => l.contains('· older') && l.contains('(5)'))
    .toList();
expect(beforeOlder, hasLength(1), reason: 'frame before:\n$before');
await harness.waitForText(_firstSettle, timeout: ...);
await harness.waitForOutput(settleMs: 300);
final mid = harness.viewportLines;
expectComposerReserved(mid, columns);
expect(
  mid.where((l) => l.contains('· older') && l.contains('(5)')).toList(),
  beforeOlder,
  reason: 'the printed `· older` row never changes counts while its jobs settle ...',

```

Line 241 is the `expect(mid.where(...), beforeOlder, ...)`. Both frames contain exactly ONE such row. The only difference: trailing spaces.

So the flake is a pure whitespace-of-buffer-cell artifact: the logical row is identical; the buffer-cell padding differs. On linux, the repaint after the settle notice produced the padded row; on macOS (different timing), the row got repainted in a way that left unpadded cells (or the line simply never got rewritten and the old line at the new scroll position wasn't padded).

Root cause class: the assertion compares raw `getText()` strings including emulator-cell padding, which is an artifact of how the TUI renderer erases/rewrites rows, not of the board's freeze semantics. The freeze assertion should compare TRIMMED content (the counts), not raw padded cells.

But wait — the test is intentionally strict ("byte-identical"). The point is the frozen snapshot must not change counts. Comparing `trimRight()`-ed lines would still catch count changes while ignoring renderer-erase artifacts. But is trimming right? Let me think about whether the trailing-space difference can hide a REAL bug. The `· older` row content is the counts; trailing padding is not content. Trimming trailing whitespace is the correct content comparison.

But hold on — is this purely a test-side artifact, or is there a real product bug where the row is repainted (unfrozen)? The counts in the row are identical ("5 running · 0 done · 0 lost") — so the freeze logic worked. The only difference is buffer padding. Let me look at the TUI rendering for the job board: lib/src/cli/fa_tui.dart, and how "live region" lines are drawn.

- `before`: full frame after wave-two turn completed. Frame rows include the board region: `⟳ Bac…

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

Let me look at the harness and understand timing.

Key timeline in the test:
1. Wave one: 5 background jobs with sleeps of 21..25 s (base 20 + i).
2. Turn 2: text reply.
3. Wave two: turn 3 with 6 jobs sleeping 300s.
4. Turn 4: text.
5. Capture `before` frame: must have exactly one `· older` row with (5).
6. Wait for first settle (`exited(0)`) — happens at base+1 = 21 s after wave one launch.
7. Capture `mid`: the `· older` row must be identical.
8. Wait for `_settledCardBody` = 'bash_job status lists ids' — the settled first wave's terminal transcript card.
9. Capture `after`: the aged row (5) must be gone from the live region, exactly one summary card, and wave two's row must show `Background jobs (6) · 6 running · 0 done · 0 lost`.

Potential flake sources on macOS (fa-m5 runners are slow):
- The comment mentions gh-937: with the original 5..9s window, the whole bucket could settle and drain BEFORE the `before` capture. Now sleeps are 21..25, so there's ~21s minimum from wave one launch to first settle. But if boot + 2 turns takes more than ~16s... wait, the sleeps start when wave one's jobs are launched (turn 1). The `before` capture happens after wave two's turn completes. If boot + turn1 + turn2 + turn3 + turn4 takes > 21 s, the first job could settle before the `before` capture. On a slow macOS runner, boot might take several seconds; each turn is a scripted stream, which should be fast, but `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` etc. Let's estimate: boot maybe 2-5s, each turn maybe 1-3s. Total maybe 15-20s worst case on a heavily loaded runner. Cutting close to 21s.

- Also, the settle time is measured from when the `sleep` command actually starts, which happens after boot + turn 1 begins executing tool calls.

- Another flake source: the "mid" assertion. After the first settle at ~21s, the remaining jobs settle at 22, 23, 24, 25 s. The `waitForOutput(settleMs: 300)` gives 300ms of quiet. Then `mid` is captured and compared with `beforeOlder`. This happens at line 241 of the test — the `mid.where(...)` equals `beforeOlder` assertion.

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... Usually `getText()` joins cell content chars; erased cells are spaces too, so both would give trailing spaces. Hmm, but the actual output shows NO trailing spaces in `mid`.

Wait — actually re-reading: Actual row has NO trailing spaces. Expected (before) has trailing spaces. So in `before`, the `· older` row was written with padding to full width; in `mid`, the row ended right after `· older` and nothing else was ever written on that row beyond that point (the rest of the buffer line was never written with spaces NOR cleared).

How can that be? The TUI repaint: full frame redraw each frame. The frame writes every row. When the board region shrinks (e.g., a settle notice removed a row?), the renderer might redraw only the changed lines and clear the remainder of a line with EL where needed, or it uses relative cursor movements to update rows in place (diff-based rendering, like dart_tui).

Then the first settle happens: `[bash] sh-1-… exited(0)` notice is appended to the transcript → the frame scrolls / repaints. Unless the whole frame scrolled: when new lines are appended at the bottom, everything scrolls up by N lines. Scrolling in the xterm emulator: `buffer.lines` shift — the top line is moved to scrollback. When a line scrolls, its content (cells) stays the same. So padding would be preserved...

Wait, actually, look more carefully: in the `before` frame, the `· older` row had trailing spaces to 120 chars. In `mid`, the row has none. The row content is the same. So between before and mid, the row was REWRITTEN without padding, or the line was cleared and rewritten.

If the cell is "unwritten" initially, the line may not be materialized at full width — the line tracks `isWrapped`/length? Let me look at the actual package.

Also there's another possibility: the TUI's renderer for the job board region uses `\x1b[K` after each line vs not. Or the renderer writes lines and pads them with spaces to full width only in SOME cases (e.g., when the line is part of the "live region" bottom panel vs the scrolling transcript).

The key question: why does the same logical row sometimes have trailing padding and sometimes not, on macOS but not linux?

So `getText()` output length depends on `_length` — the line's materialized length. A line whose cells were written with explicit spaces to column 120 has `_length` 120 and returns padded text. A line written only up to column X (length X) returns unpadded text. Also `eraseLine`/`eraseRight` typically `resize` the line: let me check buffer.dart erase functions and how resize affects length.

The mechanism for the flake:

- Frame `before`: TUI painted the full frame. The `· older` row got materialized to 120 cells (e.g., because the renderer wrote the line with padding, or because an earlier frame wrote a longer line at that row position and clear-to-end was done via spaces, or the terminal `TerminalView`... whatever) → padded text.
- Settle notice → transcript grows, screen scrolls up, board region re-renders. The renderer writes the row content, and erases the remainder of the row via `ECH`/`EL` or via writing a shorter line then `clearRight`, which SHRINKS `_length` to the written length → unpadded text.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.
- `lib/src/redact/` — laye…

A line written only up to column X (length X) returns unpadded text. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);

The COUNTS are identical — the row text is identical apart from TRAILING WHITESPACE. The `before` capture had the row padded to the full width with trailing spaces (`· older` + trailing spaces to fill the 120-column glass), while the `mid` capture has the row WITHOUT trailing padding.

This happens at line 241 of the test — the `mid.where(...)` equals `beforeOlder` assertion.

Why would trailing whitespace differ? `viewportLines` returns `buf.lines[i].getText()`. The xterm Terminal buffer keeps lines with their trailing cells. When the TUI repaints the frame, the line content depends on how the last write to that line was done:
- If the row was written with a full-width clear (spaces to end of line), the buffer cells contain spaces → `getText()` returns padded text.
- If the row was written with content and then the cursor moved / line erased with EL (erase to end of line, `\x1b[K`), the buffer cells beyond the written content are EMPTY (whitespace-width 0?) — actually in xterm emulator, `eraseToEnd` sets cells to a blank char... Let me think about the vendored xterm package behavior.

Actually in the `xterm` Dart package (vendored), `BufferLine` cells: erased cells vs written spaces may differ in `getText()` output? Usually `getText()` joins cell content chars; erased cells are spaces too, so both would give trailing spaces. Hmm, but the actual output shows NO trailing spaces in `mid`.

Wait — actually re-reading: Actual row has NO trailing spaces. Expected (before) has trailing spaces. So in `before`, the `· older` row was written with padding to full width; in `mid`, the row ended right after `· older` and nothing else was ever written on that row beyond that point (the rest of the buffer line was never written with spaces NOR cleared).

How can that be? The TUI repaint: full frame redraw each frame. The frame writes every row. When the board region shrinks (e.g., a settle notice removed a row?), the renderer might redraw only the changed lines and clear the remainder of a line with EL where needed, or it uses relative cursor movements to update rows in place (diff-based rendering, like dart_tui).

Let me think about the frame flow:

`before` was captured right after `waitForOutput(settleMs: 400)` following wave two's turn (frame complete, full repaint: all rows padded to 120 columns? Not necessarily all — the TUI's diff renderer writes only what changed but pads/clears changed rows to erase previous content).

Then the first settle happens: `[bash] sh-1-… exited(0)` notice is appended to the transcript → the frame scrolls / repaints. The `· older` row moves up by a line (the settle notice added a line above). In the new frame, the `· older` row is written WITHOUT trailing padding — because the diff renderer only wrote the changed cells (the row text), leaving the rest of the buffer line as it was (which contained... hmm, that would PRESERVE the old padding).

Unless the whole frame scrolled: when new lines are appended at the bottom, everything scrolls up by N lines. Scrolling in the xterm emulator: `buffer.lines` shift — the top line is moved to scrollback. When a line scrolls, its content (cells) stays the same. So padding would be preserved...

Wait, actually, look more carefully: in the `before` frame, the `· older` row had trailing spaces to 120 chars. In `mid`, the row has none. The row content is the same. So between before and mid, the row was REWRITTEN without padding, or the line was cleared and rewritten.

Hmm, but wait — is this really the same physical row? The screen scrolled up by ~2 lines (the settle notice block). The `· older` row in `mid` is a different buffer line — one that previously held something else. When the TUI repainted after the settle, it wrote the board row at the new position. If the renderer wrote `⟳ Background jobs (5) · 5 running · 0 done · 0 lost · older` and then cleared to end of line with EL, the emulator's erase would fill the rest with blank cells — which in getText() give spaces. If the renderer did NOT clear to EOL (e.g., it knew the old row at this position had exactly the same length? no...).

Hmm wait, actually let me reconsider: does `getText()` on the vendored xterm produce trailing spaces for erased cells? Let me check the vendored xterm implementation. In the xterm.dart package, `BufferLine` has `_buffer` with char codes and `getText()` builds from each cell's char. A "blank" cell (erased) has char code of space (0x20)? If the cell is "unwritten" initially, the line may not be materialized at full width — the line tracks `isWrapped`/length? Let me look at the actual package.

Also there's another possibility: the TUI's renderer for the job board region uses `\x1b[K` after each line vs not. Or the renderer writes lines and pads them with spaces to full width only in SOME cases (e.g., when the line is part of the "live region" bottom panel vs the scrolling transcript).

The key question: why does the same logical row sometimes have trailing padding and sometimes not, on macOS but not linux?

Actually, wait. Let me re-read the failing assertion more carefully. Test line 241:

So `getText()` output length depends on `_length` — the line's materialized length. A line whose cells were written with explicit spaces to column 120 has `_length` 120 and returns padded text. A line written only up to column X (length X) returns unpadded text. Also `eraseLine`/`eraseRight` typically `resize` the line: let me check buffer.dart erase functions and how resize affects length.

The mechanism for the flake:

- Frame `before`: TUI painted the full frame. The `· older` row got materialized to 120 cells (e.g., because the renderer wrote the line with padding, or because an earlier frame wrote a longer line at that row position and clear-to-end was done via spaces, or the terminal `TerminalView`... whatever) → padded text.
- Settle notice → transcript grows, screen scrolls up, board region re-renders. The renderer writes the row content, and erases the remainder of the row via `ECH`/`EL` or via writing a shorter line then `clearRight`, which SHRINKS `_length` to the written length → unpadded text.
